title: Drive interlocking tests through the production runners, not mocks (Bun)

facts.note: Bun discovery scope of the detector.
Only e2e test files are in scope.
Bun-stack realization; other stacks own their own renderings.
Interlocking relevance is decided by token scan of the test file content (route/train/interlocking token or runner symbol), not by path alone.
Emitted by the JS detector in the bun_interlocking_coverage family.

fires: An e2e/**/*.ts test references an interlocking route but never references TrainRunner.
An interlocking e2e test uses mock.module(...) to replace the runner module.
An interlocking e2e test defines a local resolveTrain function or *Resolver class instead of using InterlockingRunner.
An interlocking e2e test uses bun:test spyOn(...)/mock(...)/mock.restore(...) aimed at a runner.
An interlocking e2e test uses vi.spyOn/jest.spyOn to replace runner behavior (resolveTrain / execute).
doesNotFire: An e2e test with no interlocking route/train/interlocking token and no runner symbol.
A forbidden pattern that appears only inside a comment (comments are masked).
Interlocking tests in a non-Bun stack (owned by that stack's package).

given: A Bun e2e test (e2e/**/*.ts) that exercises an interlocking route or train
when: the test is written or changed to prove route/train behavior
then: Drive the production InterlockingRunner.resolveTrain -> TrainRunner.execute chain so the asserted evidence comes from the real runners, with no mock, substituted runner or hand-built resolver standing in for them.
prefer: Call `new InterlockingRunner(interlockingYamlPath).resolveTrain(action, inputs)` with guard-relevant inputs; it resolves the guarded route to exactly one `trainId`.
Pass that `trainId` to the production `TrainRunner` and execute the selected train through the real runtime path.
Assert the selected train and the route- or acceptance-specific result of its execution.
avoid: mock.module(...) on a runner module (bun:test idiom; worst case: swaps the ENTIRE route-control module).
bun:test spyOn/mock/mock.restore aimed at a runner; vi.mock/jest.mock around a runner module (migrating suites); vi.spyOn/jest.spyOn replacing runner behavior (resolveTrain/execute).
A local `resolveTrain` function or `*Resolver` class standing in for InterlockingRunner.
Importing the real runners only to satisfy the detector while assertions come from a parallel fake path.
Asserting a plan literal without driving production resolution and execution.
unless: Not an interlocking test: no interlocking route/train/interlocking token and no runner symbol.
why: A test that replaces either runner with a double exercises the double, not production route control — a descriptive green proving nothing about production.
evidence: The test references both InterlockingRunner and TrainRunner and contains none of the forbidden substitution patterns.
Breaking production `resolveTrain` or `execute` behavior would make the test red.
The asserted evidence (selected train and its execution result) comes from the real runner chain.
verifier_detail: JS detector, member of the `bun_interlocking_coverage` family; scans the consumer's interlocking-related `e2e/**/*.ts` tests with comments masked.
Check 1: the test must reference BOTH required production symbols `InterlockingRunner` and `TrainRunner`.

Check 2: any one forbidden substitution pattern is a violation: MockInterlockingRunner/MockTrainRunner; mock.module(...) replacing a runner module; spyOn(...)/mock(...)/mock.restore(...) aimed at a runner (bun:test); vi.mock(...)/jest.mock(...) around a runner module (suite migrating in); vi.spyOn(...)/jest.spyOn(...) replacing runner behavior (resolveTrain / execute); a locally defined `resolveTrain` function or `*Resolver` class standing in for InterlockingRunner.

Symbol reference is only a structural proxy, not sufficient semantic proof: a reviewer must confirm the case drives the production objects with guard-relevant inputs and observes the claimed route/train behavior.
Scope: a test is interlocking-related if it references any interlocking route/train/interlocking token or a runner symbol; otherwise out of scope.

Term production_runner: one of the two runtime objects of the core afokapu/atdd#1251 call model — InterlockingRunner (resolves a guarded route to exactly one trainId) and TrainRunner (executes the selected train).

Term forbidden_substitution (source glossary wording): a test double that replaces a production runner — MockInterlockingRunner/MockTrainRunner, a mock.module/spyOn/mock (bun:test) or vi.mock/vi.spyOn (or jest) aimed at a runner or its resolveTrain/execute, or a hand-built route resolver standing in for InterlockingRunner.
Core runtime call model (afokapu/atdd#1251): Station Master -> InterlockingRunner.resolveTrain -> TrainRunner.execute.
